chapter_title: Concerning the Fasting of the Saints

spiritual_reading.full_translation: The first practice is that a person willingly chastens the outer self by denying its cravings, and by this brings into obedience the whole governing love that had ruled within. The second is that the daily reception of life and understanding, as it is taken in through outward support and use, is to be consecrated and set in order, until it is made clean and sound, freed from the admixture of hellish evil and falsity that clings to it. The third is that the person is to make every action an act of holiness: whatever proceeds is to be in accord with the pure inner community of good and truth where there is no taint. One must not injure or profane what is received for life by bending it to corruption, but keep the inward state undefiled, so that the life within remains untroubled and at rest. The fourth is that one takes upon oneself a fixed confession of the Lord’s victorious endurance and, from it, a rule of restraint; one holds back one’s operative powers from destructive influence, so that no one violates the spiritual life in oneself or in another.

paragraph_translations.translation: The first practice is that when a holy person willingly chastens the outer self by denying its cravings, the whole governing love that rules within is subdued and brought into obedience.
paragraph_translations.connection: OPENS the spiritual teaching by establishing restraint over the ruling love.

paragraph_translations.translation: The second is that the daily reception of life and understanding, taken in through outward support, is to be made holy and set in order, until it is purified and cleared of the hellish evil and falsity that had mingled with it.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS the teaching by shifting from restraint of the ruling love to purification of daily reception.
paragraph_translations.notes: The phrase about what "comes into him" is forced into the sense of continual reception of life through external means; the exact object of reception is not fully explicit.

paragraph_translations.translation: The third is that the person makes every action holy, so that nothing proceeds except what agrees with the pure inner community of good and truth where there is no taint. One must not harm or profane what is received for life by turning it to corruption, but remain inwardly clean; thus the inner life is unpolluted and abides in peace.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by moving from cleansing reception to consecrating all outward acts.
paragraph_translations.notes: The reference to "children of light" resists direct functional naming beyond describing an inner state of untainted good and truth; the sentence fragments around corruption/defilement require smoothing.

paragraph_translations.translation: The fourth is that they take upon themselves a fixed confession of the Lord’s victorious endurance and a rule of life from it, and they restrain their operative powers in outward action from destructive use, so that the spiritual life is not violated.
paragraph_translations.connection: SHIFTS from inward purity to outward restraint for the sake of preserving spiritual life.
paragraph_translations.notes: The broken phrases make the precise action unclear; translating the "sign" as a fixed confession/rule is an interpretive necessity, and the clause about restraining hands is uncertain in detail though clear in thrust (restraint from harm).

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coherent as a fourfold progression: (1) subduing the ruling love through voluntary denial, (2) purifying daily reception of life and understanding from hellish mixture, (3) sanctifying all deeds by keeping inner good and truth untainted, and (4) establishing a rule of restraint grounded in the Lord’s deliverance so that spiritual life is preserved. The main stumble is paragraph 6’s fragmentary wording, which forces a best-fit rendering of a confession/rule leading to restraint in action.

findings.diagnosis: Clean fourfold correspondential opening: fasting is taught by what it does (subdues an interior ruling-power), not by who administers anything. No narrative seam or foreign register.
findings.evidence: Text: “Shall the holy man punish his body by fasting, he subdues the entire ruling-power that exists in him.” The spiritual reading tracks this without strain: “chastens…denying cravings… the whole governing love… is subdued.” No intrusion of lists, jurisdictions, or named authorities; the spiritual sense arises directly from the function of fasting (subduing).

findings.diagnosis: Mostly clean correspondential teaching, with a minor syntactic/lexical opacity that caused the reader’s forced gloss. The difficulty is referential (what exactly ‘comes into him… in the administration of his food’ denotes), not a voice-insertion.
findings.evidence: Text: “This soul that comes into him in the administration of his food, day by day; it shall be made holy… washed from the adulteration of the Darkness that is mixed in with it.” The spiritual reading notes the stumble: “forced into the sense… the exact object of reception is not fully explicit.” That is consistent with a transmission/translation roughness around “administration of his food” (a governance-sounding noun used in a plainly functional claim: ingestion entails mixture; fasting/purity cleanses). There is no administrative inventory, no named ranks—only the process of mixture and purification.

findings.diagnosis: Correspondential paragraph with localized damage/ellipsis. The ‘children of light’ phrase is not an administrative overlay here; it functions as a qualitative description of an uncorrupted state. The reader’s resistance comes from fragmentary syntax, not from a foreign teaching mode.
findings.evidence: Text: “make every deed a holy one; the mystery of [the children] of light in whom there is neither corruption nor [defilement]… Rather, they are holy… as they live in peace.” The reading reports: “resists direct functional naming… sentence fragments… require smoothing.” That matches the bracketed lacunae ([children], [defilement]) and the broken clause “the food, nor wound it,” which looks like a damaged line rather than a different voice. No jurisdictions/authorities are assigned; the teaching still proceeds by state (uncorrupted/undefiled → peace).

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty from damaged text and compressed ritual language, producing an interpretive patch (‘sign upon the Cross’ → ‘fixed confession/rule’). This is not a clear administrative insertion; it remains an action-and-effect admonition (mark/sign → restraint of hands → not destroying the living soul).
findings.evidence: Text is visibly broken: “They make a [sign upon] the Cross, they restrain their hands from the hand [that he may] destroy the living soul.” The spiritual reading explicitly flags the stumble: “broken phrases… translating the ‘sign’ as a fixed confession/rule is an interpretive necessity… clause… uncertain in detail.” Despite the obscurity, the logic is functional (a sign/practice leads to restraint, preventing harm to the living soul) and lacks the administrative markers (named rulers, stations, authority lists). Removing it would not reveal a smoother administrative/correspondential seam; it would simply delete the chapter’s fourth item.

textual_criticism.summary: No administrative overlay or insertion detected. The chapter is a coherent fourfold correspondential teaching on fasting (effects: subduing inner rule, purifying daily intake from mixture, sanctifying deeds in an uncorrupted state, restraining harmful action). The spiritual reading ‘stumbles’ in ¶4–¶6 due to referential opacity and clear textual damage/bracketing, not because an administrative Mani-layer has been inserted. Recommendations: 0 excisions, 0 annotations, 4 none (with ¶6 diagnosed as damaged).

harmonized_paragraphs.text: The first work: Shall the holy man punish his body by fasting, he subdues the entire ruling-power that exists in him.

The second: This soul that comes into him in the administration of his food, day by day; it shall be made holy, cleansed, purified, and washed from the adulteration of the Darkness that is mixed in with it.

The third: That person shall make every deed a holy one; the mystery of [the children] of light in whom there is neither corruption nor [defilement] the food, nor wound it. Rather, they are holy, [there is nothing] in them that defiles, as they live in peace.
The fourth: They make a [sign upon] the Cross, they restrain their hands from the hand [that he may] destroy the living soul.

changes_summary: No changes made. All findings (¶3–¶6) carried a recommendation of none; therefore no excisions were executed, and no paragraphs were modified.
